hypothesis: On x86 CPUs with AVX and SSSE3 but no AVX2 or FMA (Sandy Bridge, Ivy Bridge) the planar int4 expert dot runs the SSE2 int16 kernel; an AVX tier (PMADDUBSW + PMADDWD, the emulated fmaf in four double lanes with a short way where the double sum is not a float's midpoint, two weight rows interleaved) should cut the routed experts' time and raise decode speed with the same bits.
model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kreuzzelg/qwen36-35b-a3b-colibri-i4-gs64 (int4 gs=64 safetensors container from the one-step setup)
command: make -C c qwen36 ARCH=native in a worktree of each commit; python3 docs/experiments/qwen36-avx-i8-2026-11-17/bench.py MODEL OUT dev:WT_DEV/c avx:WT_AVX/c, once per pair, three pairs (each run: coli serve --model MODEL --auto-tier --port 8011, one warm-up request, three timed requests, five others, the same three again; tok_s holds the second round)

hardware.cpu: 2x Intel Xeon E5-2670 (Sandy Bridge-EP: AVX, SSSE3, no AVX2, no FMA, no F16C), 16 cores / 32 threads, 2 NUMA nodes
hardware.ram: 94 GiB DDR3, 64 GB on node 0 and 32 GB on node 1
hardware.storage: 7200 rpm HDD, ext4 (rw,relatime); the model was in the page cache for every run

quality.method: tests/test_xf_avx_i8 (the kernel through the dispatch against the reference loop, both fmaf forms against libm) and tests/test_expert_ffn pass on this CPU; the text of the six timed replies is byte-identical in all six runs (sha256 9ec0f3c7a6ffae4888f65424209f872fb43178efcb3d64132ef3cb1d007d58eb)
